utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, everyone. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-9-A, the Prosecutor versus Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, can you hear and follow proceedings in a language that you can understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances, please. First of all the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Steffen Wirth appearing for the Prosecution, together with Senior Appeals Counsel Norman Farrell, and our case manager today is Ms. Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I'm turning to the Defence, Mr. Simic's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Igor Pantelic, a lawyer in Belgrade, and my colleague is going to introduce himself straight away. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. Peter Murphy for the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is a Status Conference organised in line with Article 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the International Tribunal. According to that, as I was saying, a Status Conference should be held within 120 days following the launching of an appeal, then once again every 120 days, giving the appellant the possibility to raise any issues of importance, including information about the appellant's mental and physical health. In this case, Mr. Simic launched an appeal against the sentence passed on the 17th of October, 2003. All of the submissions were submitted, and this is the fifth Status Conference with regard to this appeal. Mr. Simic, or perhaps the Defence on behalf of Mr. Simic, would you like to raise any issues pertaining to the conditions of detention or the defendant's state of health? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no objections to the conditions at the Detention Unit, and at the moment I have no health issues to report to you either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You may sit down. As to the state of progress of this appeal, all of the submissions have been filed, and there are no requests pending at the moment before the Trial Chamber. No date has been set as yet for an appeal hearing. So I don't have any special issues to address. Parties may have comments, so I would like to know whether you have any comments or any questions. The Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have nothing to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is one matter that I will mention tentatively, not knowing whether it will be of importance or not. Your Honour may be aware that of the decision in the case of Radoslav Brdjanin, on the Prosecution's -- the motion to dismiss ground 1 of the Prosecutor's appeal, which was issued by the President on the 5th of May, 2005, Your Honour, this decision deals with certain aspects of the law relating to joint criminal enterprise, specifically the issue as to whether a joint criminal enterprise must include the physical perpetrators of the criminal acts. The President called on the Association of Defence Counsel to present an amicus curiae brief on that issue. Your Honour, Mr. Pantelic and I have not yet had the opportunity of reviewing that brief, nor do we know whether it has been filed, but -- and it may be that it raises no issues directly related to our case, but clearly the President has indicated that it is a matter of some importance, because even though it was not pursued by the Prosecution before the Trial Chamber in the Brdjanin case, it was ruled to be a question which may affect the jurisprudence of the Tribunal and one which, therefore, the Appeals Chamber would consider. Your Honour, if -- if it should be the case that this issue is in some way relevant to this appeal, we might want to take the opportunity to mention that before the hearing of this case so that judicial time is not consumed unduly in hearing the issues when perhaps they might be heard with greater precision at a later date. Your Honour, as soon as we are in a position to address the Court on that question, if it does appear necessary, we may seek leave to file an appropriate motion at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. As you've just indicated, it may well be that the matter you've raised does not really have a direct link to today's case, but if I'm not mistaken, we still do not have a finalised report on that. So I have taken note of what you've just said, and I believe that's all we can do for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Since there don't seem to be any other issues pending, this Status Conference can now be adjourned.
